title: The supported product is invariant under equality of closed supports
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, f:X→S and g:Y→S scheme morphisms, i:Z→X and i′:Z′→X closed immersions with the same open complement, and j:W→Y and j′:W′→Y closed immersions with the same open complement. For arbitrary unbounded etale A-module complexes K on X and L on Y, the actual product [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] for (i,j,K,L) is invertible if and only if that for (i′,j′,K,L) is invertible. Supports and derived support functors are as in [def-pur-support-cohomology] and [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. No reducedness or boundedness assumption is made.

proof.text: Equal open complements identify the kernels defining support sections and their inclusions into global sections, hence also their right derived functors. The normalized supported-coefficient adjunctions therefore have identified right adjoints. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives an isomorphism of supported coefficient functors. Their quotient maps from constant coefficients agree under this isomorphism by the normalization of the Hom bijections. This is the ordinary kernel identification underlying the derived support congruence in [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle].

The product supports have equal complements: their underlying closed sets are the intersections of the inverse images of the two specified closed sets. Under the coefficient isomorphisms the two coefficient tensor comparisons agree: precompose with the tensor of the constant-to-support quotients, use their defining constant-tensor equations, and cancel this epimorphism. Signed total-complex comparisons agree on every bidegree inclusion. Their derived comparison families agree by the cochain-model normalization and naturality of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product].

Adjunction uniqueness makes the two evaluation counits commute with these isomorphisms. Transpose the tensor of their evaluations under the product-support adjunction. The resulting supported products are conjugate by the supported-section isomorphisms on their sources and targets, so their invertibility is equivalent. The same calculation includes empty and full supports and arbitrary shifts.

theorem isIso_supportedExteriorProduct_iff_supportComplement_eq
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] {S X Y Z Z' W W' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X)
    (j : W ⟶ Y) (j' : W' ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion i']
    [IsClosedImmersion j] [IsClosedImmersion j']
    (hi : i.openComplement = i'.openComplement)
    (hj : j.openComplement = j'.openComplement)
    (K : DerivedCategoryModule A X) (L : DerivedCategoryModule A Y) :
    IsIso (supportedExteriorProduct A f g i j K L) ↔
      IsIso (supportedExteriorProduct A f g i' j' K L)
